name: Energy audits and efficiency surveys
one_line: The operator's own file for how much energy a site or named system uses and what would reduce it: a defined energy boundary, a measured baseline of consumption or intensity, the walkthrough and meter evidence that built the baseline, and the opportunity register of efficiency measures with estimated savings and payback. Its anchor is a surveyed energy system and a baseline period — not a product lot, not a maintained asset's work order, not a utility supplier's bill, and not a statutory emissions scheme return. Placeholder template on the fieldless manufacturing schema; researched to J-DEPTH.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: No canonical key names the surveyed consumption boundary of an energy study. The manufacturing schema's proposed `asset` is one maintained machine (CNC-07, Boiler B-3); an energy audit routinely scopes a functional system that spans many assets and distribution (compressed air, HVAC, steam, lighting, Line 2 ovens). `location` is the Photos capture-location role and may differ from the system the readings describe. `project` is bounded work rather than a recurring consumption boundary that several audits revisit over years. This key should hold a labelled System, Energy System, Boundary, End Use or Survey Scope slot, never an organisation name or an inferred topic.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE beneath site because opportunity sheets, meter exports and thermal surveys are unintelligible without the system they cover; the template validator should flatten when a corpus holds exactly one system.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Direct from a labelled System/Boundary/End-use/Scope slot on an audit or baseline sheet. Free-text names stay possible because the same words appear in maintenance manuals and capital proposals. A validated ceiling would need a local system register plus labelled-role context; R4/R6 own that rule family.
proposed_fields.note_for_r1c: R1c may fold this into `asset` with a role qualifier. The argument against is the multi-asset system boundary; the counter-argument that a named boiler plant is an asset is real and recorded as NJ-MEA-2.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: REUSE of the proposal already argued on `manufacturing.environmental-compliance`, not a new spelling. No canonical key names the interval a baseline or survey covers. `term` is Academic, `tax_year` is Finance, `capture_year` is Photos, and `creation_date` is when the file was made — routinely a different interval from the baseline year. This key must carry the covered interval from a labelled Baseline Period, Survey Period, Reporting Period or Audit Period slot.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Proposed TRUE as a leaf-adjacent level only. The baseline interval is a subject here, not a timestamp, because savings are defined against it. It is still NOT proposed as a first dimension.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Direct from a labelled period slot; possible from a filename token such as 2025 Baseline, which is ambiguous with a financial year and a document version. Never validated alone.
proposed_fields.note_for_r1c: Prefer one global period key shared with environmental-compliance rather than minting `audit_period` or `baseline_period`.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: REUSE of the contested manufacturing-schema proposal (NJ-MFG-1), not a new spelling. If R1c widens the canonical Finance `record_type` into a global document-function key, this row adopts it as a leaf beneath site, energy system and period.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Inherited if reuse is approved; normally a leaf.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: Explicit document titles and labelled form headers support the value; filenames and isolated words do not.

deterministic: an energy-audit or energy-review structure that names a site or installation, defines an energy boundary or system scope, states a baseline period, and presents measured consumption or intensity for that scope; the boundary-plus-baseline-plus-measurement relation is the signal, not the words energy or audit alone

an opportunity or ECM register whose rows pair a named measure with estimated energy savings, estimated cost and a payback or simple-return figure, tied to one site or energy system; a capital-project list without savings/payback against a measured baseline does not satisfy this structure

an interval or cumulative meter-data export whose columns carry a meter or end-use identity, timestamps or billing periods, and energy quantity (kWh, therms, MJ, steam mass), used as baseline evidence for a labelled site or system rather than as a supplier invoice
a walkthrough or end-use survey sheet with equipment or fixture inventories, nameplate or operating data, hours-of-use or load estimates, and a link to one energy system under survey

a combustion, boiler, chiller, compressed-air or motor efficiency test sheet with measured input, useful output or specific power, and an efficiency or intensity result for one named system — not a product inspection against a drawing tolerance
a lighting, HVAC or steam-trap survey table whose rows are fixtures or traps with condition, measured reading and a recommended action that feeds an opportunity register
an energy-balance or Sankey workbook that allocates site total energy across labelled end uses for one baseline period
an EnMS or ISO 50001 energy-review extract that states significant energy uses, EnPIs and a baseline, without being merely a downloaded copy of the standard text
an email whose labelled subject names an energy audit, baseline, ECM or opportunity register for an identified site or system and whose attachments are audit, meter or opportunity records

an archive whose manifest links one site or energy-system token across a baseline workbook, walkthrough sheets, thermal images and an opportunity register for one survey; the manifest is read without unpacking the archive to disk
needs_llm: a spreadsheet of kWh figures with no header block, which could be a supplier settlement, a process-control log, a GHG activity-data sheet or an energy baseline
a GHG inventory workbook whose verification tab and savings tab pull the same meters in opposite directions
a consultancy slide deck that mixes sales claims with measured site data, where the measured boundary may or may not be separable
an OCR-poor walkthrough form where equipment tags survive visually but column labels do not
a thermal image of a steam line or facade with no visible tag, system label or accompanying survey sheet
a multilingual EnMS form whose baseline and SEU labels are absent from the deterministic context catalogue
a home or small-office energy certificate that may be personal-property evidence rather than a manufacturing-site survey
never_alone: the word energy, audit, efficiency, kWh, therm, sustainability, net-zero, carbon, EnMS, ECM or retrofit alone

an organisation name alone — a utility, an ESCO, a consultancy, a certification body or ENERGY STAR; an organisation name is never-alone evidence and identifies the issuer or the advisor, not the surveyed system
an ISO 50001, ASHRAE or equivalent standard designation alone; a downloaded copy of a standard is a reference document, not evidence that the holder ran a survey under it
a meter number, account number, serial number or asset tag outside a labelled role slot
a savings percentage, payback figure, date or signature alone
a source_type or extension alone; spreadsheets, PDFs, images, email and archives occur in every neighbouring row
a download session alone: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic"
a parent folder called Energy, Sustainability, Utilities, ESG or HSE alone
missing EXIF as proof that a plant photograph or thermal image is a screenshot: "the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot"
a utility bill, invoice or payment confirmation alone; those prove a transaction until a baseline boundary and measured end-use structure independently support this row

grouping_reasons: one site across baseline, walkthrough, meter exports and opportunity registers for the same survey
one energy system across efficiency tests, leak surveys and the ECM rows that reference it
one baseline period across the meter exports and the report that consumes them
one opportunity register across implementation evidence that cites the same measure identifiers
duplicate and version families remain universal facts and never manufacture site, system or period facts by propagation

template.why: Empty by placeholder contract because the manufacturing schema declares no canonical fields. The recommendation held as prose is site → energy_system → reporting_period → record_type. That is deliberately unlike the schema default's product → batch_lot → record_type and site → asset → record_type branches: an energy survey of a compressed-air system has no product and no lot, and filing it under a single compressor asset would split the distribution and end-use evidence that make the baseline intelligible. Period is leaf-adjacent, not first: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Parent context still follows "a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child" — an ECM row is meaningless without the system and baseline it was sized against. The user may reverse, remove or flatten after facts are validated.

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `2026 GHG inventory - Scope 1 and 2 - Plant 2.xlsx` — this row owns consumption profiling, end-use allocation, efficiency measures, payback and savings against a measured baseline; the neighbour owns the statutory or scheme reporting frame — registration or permit reference, organisational boundary for the scheme, reporting period and independent verification opinion; discriminated by whether the activating structure is the savings/ECM/baseline-efficiency apparatus or the verification/scheme apparatus. When both structures are present on disjoint tabs they coexist rather than compete, matching that row's own edge and NJ-MEC-3.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Boiler B-3 combustion efficiency test 2026-03-12.pdf` beside `WO-9102 Boiler B-3 burner cleaning.xml` — this row owns the measured efficiency or intensity result against a surveyed energy system and baseline; the neighbour owns the asset work order with failure or task code, work performed, parts or labour and returned-to-service status; discriminated by efficiency/baseline/ECM structure versus work-order execution structure. A boiler identity alone activates neither.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Plant 2 - 15min interval kWh - Meter M-17 - 2025.csv` — this row owns the operator-side use of meter quantities as baseline or end-use evidence inside an energy boundary and survey; the neighbour owns the supplier-side metering and billing operations that produce settlement quantities for an account; discriminated by survey/baseline/ECM context versus account/settlement/billing context. Interval columns alone discriminate neither.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Electricity bill - Plant 2 - Feb 2026.pdf` — this row does not activate on a bill; the finance row owns the account, billing period, charges and amount due as a recurring utility record; discriminated by presence of a payment/charges block without an energy boundary or ECM register (finance/residual) versus boundary-plus-baseline-plus-opportunity structure (this row). A plant name and a kWh total on a bill are never enough here.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Commissioning report - AHU-4 performance test.pdf` — this row owns a multi-period baseline and opportunity analysis for an operating energy system; the neighbour owns design-versus-actual performance at handover with witness and acceptance; discriminated by baseline-period end-use or ECM structure versus handover acceptance structure. One-time commissioning readings are not an energy audit.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: an ISO 50001 surveillance report covering document control, competence and energy-review clauses under one numbering — this row owns the energy-review findings that cite a measured baseline, significant energy uses or an opportunity register; the neighbour owns the organisational-control audit as a whole, including inseparable integrated-system findings; discriminated by whether the activating evidence is the measured energy apparatus or the management-system clause apparatus. Abstain on the report as a whole when the two cannot be separated.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Lighting inventory - Warehouse A - survey 2026-02.xlsx` — this row owns an end-use energy inventory with wattage, hours and estimated kWh feeding an ECM; the neighbour owns a property or works survey under a professional instruction about the building or site condition; discriminated by energy-quantity and savings structure versus property/works instruction structure. The word survey alone activates neither.

also_holds_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: an ECM that includes a scrubber, heat-recovery or control-sequence design attachment — this row owns the measured baseline and the savings/payback justification; engineering owns the design revision, calculation or P&ID that would implement the measure. Disjoint evidence; neither copies its anchor onto the other.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Compressed air system - baseline and ECM register.xlsx` — this row owns the measured baseline and opportunity sizing; business_operations may own the programme tracker, owner and due-date workflow that implements the same measure ids when those management slots are present on disjoint evidence.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: a workbook that pastes utility-bill line items into a baseline sheet — finance owns the bill's charges and account facts from the invoice block; this row owns the end-use allocation and savings analysis built from the quantities. "One file may hold facts from more than one domain without losing information." Quantities are not copied onto a sparse invoice merely because the files group.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Plant 2 - 15min interval kWh - Meter M-17 - 2025.csv` — when the same export carries both settlement identity for utility operations and labelled baseline/end-use context for a site energy survey, each schema activates from its own slots on disjoint evidence.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `FLIR_8841_steam_header.jpg` — Photos owns capture-time and camera facts; this row activates only when accompanying survey text or an exact system reference in the packet ties the image to an energy survey. Image bytes alone stay with Photos or One-Off Images.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone efficiency certificate, one-off test sheet or survey PDF with durable purpose but insufficient site, energy-system or baseline evidence remains "standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group".

A utility bill, ESCO invoice or payment confirmation proves a transaction rather than a surveyed baseline; 00's residual for "isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records" is the correct home.
A downloaded standard, vendor brochure or generic efficiency article with no site baseline is reading material, not a survey record.

A kWh spreadsheet or GHG workbook whose scheme-versus-savings role remains ambiguous is a file "whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision". Abstain rather than guess between this row and environmental-compliance.
An encrypted audit pack or unreadable meter-logger binary is represented without inferring an energy system from its filename.
A thermal or plant photograph with no survey label, system marker or accompanying sheet carries no energy-system evidence of its own.

sensitivity_why: Load profiles, specific energy consumption, leak losses and opportunity registers can disclose process intensity, operating schedules and commercially valuable savings pathways. Utility account numbers and meter identifiers are account-adjacent. Named technicians and auditors remain search and privacy observations, never destination dimensions — "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension." This row assigns no handling class; P7 owns that vocabulary and privacy policy must run before any model or connector.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-MEA-1 (joint with NJ-MEC-3): is the discriminator between this row and manufacturing.environmental-compliance the statutory-scheme frame versus the efficiency/baseline frame argued on both sides, or should carbon/GHG reporting be pulled to its own row (not recommended here — that would be a topic word)? NJ-MEA-2: is `energy_system` distinct from manufacturing `asset`, or should R1c fold system boundaries into asset with a role qualifier? NJ-MEA-3: should `reporting_period` be one global period key shared with environmental-compliance, or does a baseline-year need a differently named key? NJ-MEA-4: inherits NJ-MFG-1 on `record_type` reuse. Until R1c answers, this placeholder correctly declares fields: [] and dimension_order: [].
